embeds.description:
**Actor:** North Korean actors, TeamPCP
The article discusses supply chain attacks targeting CI/CD processes, including a March 2026 incident where North Korean actors hijacked an Axios npm library maintainer's account and published malicious versions downloaded by approximately 3% of the userbase. Separately, TeamPCP reportedly compromised Aqua's Trivy vulnerability scanner, BerriAI's LiteLLM, and Checkmarx/kics in February/March 2026. Mercor claims to be 'one of thousands of companies impacted' by the LiteLLM supply chain attack, and the European Commission reportedly lost 300GB of data via an API key compromised in the Trivy attack. The article proposes build application firewalls (BAF) as a solution to detect malicious code in CI/CD processes.
**Sources:** SecurityWeek • 🟡 2 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** Compromised npm library maintainer account; compromised vulnerability scanner and development tools
